claims.text: Intrinsic nanoscale lattice distortions promote the formation of sub-micron ferromagnetic clusters in rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys.
Sub-micron ferromagnetic clusters facilitate a strong magnetocaloric effect at low applied fields.
The proposed distortion-and-cluster microstructure sustains rapid heat exchange.
The proposed distortion-and-cluster microstructure sustains low hysteresis.
The proposed distortion-and-cluster microstructure sustains mechanical stability.
The as-cast equiatomic alloy has a homogeneous overall composition while exhibiting nanoscale lattice distortions.
The as-cast alloy exhibits emerging local compositional heterogeneity.
Controlled thermal annealing can progressively reduce nanoscale lattice distortions without altering the bulk composition.
Controlled thermal annealing can progressively reduce local compositional inhomogeneity without altering the bulk composition.
The ferromagnetic clusters lower energy barriers for magnetic reorientation.
Lower magnetic-reorientation barriers enable a pronounced and reversible low-field magnetocaloric response.
Lower magnetic-reorientation barriers minimize magnetic hysteresis.
A mechanically coherent matrix maintains efficient heat exchange.
Annealed samples with reduced nanoscale heterogeneity will have a lower low-field magnetocaloric response than the as-cast baseline.
Annealed samples with reduced nanoscale heterogeneity will have higher coercivity and enhanced hysteresis relative to the as-cast baseline.
Annealing will cause only modest changes in heat-transfer efficiency relative to the as-cast baseline.
The proposed relationships apply to equiatomic, transition-metal-based, rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys with significant atomic-size mismatch at fields up to approximately 0.5 T.

contradictions.description: The prediction calls for only modest changes in heat-transfer efficiency, whereas the falsification rule treats a significant alteration in heat-exchange rates as part of the expected combined response.
